# stream

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/stream"
```

Package stream is the public facade for the SDK's durable, partitioned, offset-addressed log: a producer appends records, and any number of consumer groups read every one of them, each at its own pace, until the stream's retention removes it (ADR 0231).

```
s, err := stream.NewFile(stream.FileConfig{
	Dir:    "/var/lib/myapp/orders",
	Policy: stream.Policy{Partitions: 8, RetainFor: 7 * 24 * time.Hour},
})

// …in the producer: one batch, one partition, one sync.
appended, err := s.Append(ctx, []stream.Record{{Key: orderID, Payload: body}})

// …in each consumer group, possibly in another process:
err = stream.Subscribe(ctx, s, stream.SubscriberConfig{
	Group:               "billing",
	Handler:             bill, // one partition's records, in offset order
	HandlerIsIdempotent: true, // required; see below
})
```

### This is not a queue, and the difference is the whole design

pkg/v1/data/queue and this package both carry bytes from one process to another, durably. They keep them for opposite reasons:

```
                  | queue                      | stream (this package)
------------------|----------------------------|---------------------------
A record is kept  | until a consumer acks it   | until its retention ends
Readers           | compete for each message   | every group reads every one
Position          | a lease the broker holds   | an offset the reader names
Order             | none past the first retry  | per partition, per key
Replay            | impossible: Ack removed it | read from an older offset
A failing record  | dead-lettered, others pass | blocks its partition, or is
                  |                            | parked by the subscriber
Backpressure      | none on Publish            | MaxBytes, then STREAM_FULL
```

If several workers should share a pile of jobs and each job be done once, you want a queue. If several independent readers — billing, search, an audit — must each see every record, in order, and a new reader must be able to start from the beginning, you want a stream.

### Keys, partitions and order

A record's partition is its key's, by [PartitionOf](#PartitionOf): FNV-1a modulo [Policy](#Policy).Partitions, the same on every engine, so the records of one key are read in the order they were appended wherever they are kept. Order holds within a partition and nowhere else. An [Stream](#Stream).Append is one batch on one partition under one sync: records whose keys hash apart are refused with [PartitionsMixed](#PartitionsMixed), and a batch of unkeyed records is spread round-robin. [Policy](#Policy).Partitions cannot change for the life of a stream: a key's partition is its hash modulo that number.

### Reading is by offset, and nothing is removed by reading

[Stream](#Stream).Read returns the entries of one partition from an offset, at most max of them, and returns at once — empty at the end. [Stream](#Stream).Bounds says the first offset still retained and the next one to be assigned; a read below the first is [OffsetTrimmed](#OffsetTrimmed), past the next [OffsetAhead](#OffsetAhead). The siblings, reached by type assertion on every engine here, do the rest: a [Waker](#Waker) signal ends an idle reader's wait on the next Append in this process, a [Seeker](#Seeker) turns an instant into an offset, a [Trimmer](#Trimmer) drops a partition's prefix, a [Compactor](#Compactor) keeps the last record of each key and a [Committer](#Committer) keeps each group's offset.

### A consumer group commits its offset, at least once by default

[Subscribe](#Subscribe) runs one worker per partition for a group, hands the handler the partition's records in offset order, and commits the offset after a batch the handler accepted. A crash between the handler's return and that commit delivers the batch again, so [SubscriberConfig](#SubscriberConfig).HandlerIsIdempotent must be true: its zero is refused, as the queue's is. A handler that keeps failing blocks its partition and only its partition — that is what per-key order costs —, unless [SubscriberConfig](#SubscriberConfig).Park sends the record to a queue as a dead letter and moves on.

### Exactly once in effect, in your own database

[NewSQL](#NewSQL) keeps the stream in three tables of the database your application already writes, created by [SQLMigration](#SQLMigration). An Append made inside your transaction is a savepoint of it: its records exist if and only if your transaction commits, which makes the stream an outbox. Under [CommitByHandler](#CommitByHandler) the handler commits the group's offset itself, through the stream's [Committer](#Committer), in the transaction that holds its effect: the effect and the offset commit or roll back together — exactly once in effect, the one guarantee no transport alone can give.

### Retention, backpressure and compaction

[Policy](#Policy).RetainFor and [Policy](#Policy).RetainBytes bound what a partition keeps; zero keeps everything. [Policy](#Policy).MaxBytes bounds the whole stream: above it an Append waits up to [Policy](#Policy).BlockTimeout for retention to free room, then is refused with [StreamFull](#StreamFull). A [Compactor](#Compactor) keeps a key's last record and drops the older ones — a record with a key and no payload is a tombstone — leaving their offsets as holes a read skips, never renumbered.

### Three engines

[NewFile](#NewFile) keeps the stream in a directory of segments, one log per partition, and survives the process; one engine opens a directory at a time. [NewSQL](#NewSQL) keeps it in your database, joined to your transaction. [NewMemory](#NewMemory) is the test double: the port's full semantics and the same refusals, through the same guard, with nothing that survives the process.

<a name="NewFile"></a>
## func [NewFile](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func NewFile(cfg FileConfig) (s Stream, err error)
```

NewFile opens the durable stream kept in cfg.Dir, creating it when absent, and recovers it: one segmented log per partition and the groups' cursors.

It refuses at construction a policy it cannot honour, a directory it cannot trust or another engine holds open ([StreamDirectoryUnusable](#StreamDirectoryUnusable)), and a segment it cannot trust ([StreamBackendFailed](#StreamBackendFailed)). Where the disk filesystem of package vfs does not exist — Windows, illumos and Solaris (ADR 0018) — it refuses with proc.UnsupportedPlatform, before anything else: the groups' cursors are kept there. The stream also answers io.Closer by type assertion, which releases the directory:

```
if closer, ok := s.(io.Closer); ok { defer closer.Close() }
```

<a name="NewMemory"></a>
## func [NewMemory](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func NewMemory(cfg MemoryConfig) (s Stream, err error)
```

NewMemory returns the in-process test double: the port's full semantics, its five siblings, no directory and nothing that survives the process. It refuses the policies every engine refuses, through the same guard.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

ExampleNewMemory appends two records under one key and reads them back from the partition the key hashes to, in the order they were appended.

```go
ctx := context.Background()
s, err := stream.NewMemory(stream.MemoryConfig{Policy: stream.Policy{Partitions: 4}})
if err != nil {
	return
}
key := []byte("order-42")
appended, err := s.Append(ctx, []stream.Record{{Key: key, Payload: []byte("placed")}, {Key: key, Payload: []byte("paid")}})
if err != nil {
	return
}
fmt.Println(appended.Partition == stream.PartitionOf(key, s.Partitions()), appended.First, appended.Last)
entries, err := s.Read(ctx, appended.Partition, appended.First, 10)
if err != nil {
	return
}
for _, e := range entries {
	fmt.Println(e.Offset, string(e.Record.Payload))
}
```

#### Output

```
true 0 1
0 placed
1 paid
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="NewSQL"></a>
## func [NewSQL](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func NewSQL(cfg SQLConfig) (s Stream, err error)
```

NewSQL returns a stream kept in three tables of the caller's database, created by [SQLMigration](#SQLMigration). An Append or a Commit inside a transaction its context carries for cfg.Transactor is a savepoint of it, and the [Waker](#Waker) fires only once that transaction commits. It sends no statement.

It refuses at construction a policy it cannot honour, a RetainBytes or a MaxBytes it does not keep, and a transactor, dialect or table it cannot use ([SQLStreamMisconfigured](#SQLStreamMisconfigured)). The transactor must be the SDK's, or another sql Joiner and Deferrer.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

ExampleNewSQL keeps the stream in the caller's database: the Append joins the transaction the order is written in, so the record exists if and only if the order does, and a handler under CommitByHandler commits its group's offset in the transaction that holds its own effect — exactly once in effect.

```go
ctx := context.Background()
var db *stdsql.DB
tm, err := sql.NewTransactor(sql.Config{DB: db, Dialect: sql.DialectPostgres})
if err != nil {
	return
}
_, err = stream.SQLMigration(sql.DialectPostgres, "app_orders", 20261112120000)
if err != nil {
	return
}
orders, err := stream.NewSQL(stream.SQLConfig{Transactor: tm, Dialect: sql.DialectPostgres, Table: "app_orders"})
if err != nil {
	return
}
err = tm.Transact(ctx, sql.TxOptions{}, func(ctx context.Context, ex sql.Executor) error {
	if _, err := ex.ExecContext(ctx, "INSERT INTO orders (id) VALUES ($1)", "42"); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err := orders.Append(ctx, [ // the application's pool, opened with its driver
	]stream.Record{{Key: []byte("42"), Payload: []byte("placed")}})
	return err
})
if err != nil {
	return
}
_ = stream.Subscribe(ctx, orders, stream.SubscriberConfig{Group: "invoices", Commit: stream.CommitByHandler, HandlerIsIdempotent: true, Handler: func(ctx context.Context, entries []stream.Entry) error {
	return tm.Transact(ctx, sql.TxOptions{}, func(ctx context.Context, ex sql.Executor) error {
		if _, err := ex.ExecContext(ctx, "INSERT INTO invoices (order_id) VALUES ($1)", string(entries[0].Record.Key)); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		last := entries[len(entries)-1]
		return orders.(stream.Committer).Commit(ctx, "invoices", last.Partition, last.Offset+1)
	})
}})
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="PartitionOf"></a>
## func [PartitionOf](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func PartitionOf(key []byte, partitions int) int
```

PartitionOf returns the partition a record keyed key is appended to among partitions: the 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the key modulo partitions, the placement every engine applies. A partitions below one is read as one.

<a name="SQLMigration"></a>
## func [SQLMigration](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func SQLMigration(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
```

SQLMigration returns the migration that creates the three tables an SQL stream named table keeps on dialect — table, table\_\_heads and table\_\_cursors —, numbered version for the caller's own version table. Its Down drops them, and every record and cursor in them. Its statements do nothing when the tables exist.

<a name="Subscribe"></a>
## func [Subscribe](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Subscribe(ctx context.Context, s Stream, cfg SubscriberConfig) error
```

Subscribe reads s on behalf of the consumer group cfg.Group until ctx ends: one worker per partition, each handing cfg.Handler the partition's records in offset order and moving the group's offset past each batch the handler accepted. A worker starts at the offset the group committed, or at the partition's first retained one.

A batch the handler refuses is handed back after cfg.Retry's wait, and its partition goes no further until it is accepted or, with cfg.Park, parked; the other partitions carry on. A batch accepted as the stop lands is still committed, within cfg.SettleTimeout.

It returns nil when ctx ends, [SubscriberMisconfigured](#SubscriberMisconfigured) for a configuration it cannot run, and the storage's error when the stream, the park's queue or the fence refuses. cfg.HandlerIsIdempotent must be true; see the package documentation.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

ExampleSubscribe reads a stream on behalf of the group "billing": the handler gets the partition's records in offset order, and the group's offset is committed past every batch it accepted.

```go
s, err := stream.NewMemory(stream.MemoryConfig{Policy: stream.Policy{Partitions: 1}})
if err != nil {
	return
}
for _, payload := range []string{"a", "b", "c"} {
	if _, err := s.Append(context.Background(), []stream.Record{{Payload: []byte(payload)}}); err != nil {
		return
	}
}
ctx, stop := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
seen := 0
err = stream.Subscribe(ctx, s, stream.SubscriberConfig{Group: "billing", Handler: func(_ context.Context, entries []stream.Entry) error {
	for _, e := range entries {
		fmt.Println(e.Offset, string(e.Record.Payload))
		seen++
	}
	if seen == 3 {
		stop()
	}
	return nil
}, HandlerIsIdempotent: true})
fmt.Println("subscribe:", err)
next, err := s.(stream.Committer).Committed(context.Background(), "billing", 0)
fmt.Println("committed:", next, err)
```

#### Output

```
0 a
1 b
2 c
subscribe: <nil>
committed: 3 <nil>
```

</p>
</details>

## type [Appended](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

Appended is the public alias for what [Stream](#Stream).Append answers: the partition the batch went to and the offsets of its first and last records.

```go

```

Appended is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/stream.AppendValue`, declared as:

<a name="Committer"></a>
## type [Committer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

Committer is the public alias for the sibling that keeps each consumer group's offset per partition. On [NewSQL](#NewSQL) a Commit made inside the caller's transaction commits with it.

```go

```

Committer is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/stream.Committer`, declared as:

```go
type Committer interface {
	// Commit records next as the offset group reads next on partition,
	// replacing whatever the group committed there before — moving it back is
	// legitimate: it is a replay. next past the partition's next offset is
	// [OffsetAhead]; below its first retained offset it is kept, and the
	// group's next Read reports [OffsetTrimmed]. An empty group is
	// [StreamMisconfigured]; a partition outside [0, Partitions()) is
	// [UnknownPartition].
	Commit(ctx context.Context, group string, partition int, next Offset) error
	// Committed returns the offset group committed last on partition.
	//
	// A group that never committed there is [UnknownGroup] — never a zero
	// offset, because "start at the beginning" and "start at the end" are both
	// legitimate first positions and only the reader knows which it wants.
	Committed(ctx context.Context, group string, partition int) (Offset, error)
}
```

An empty group is [StreamMisconfigured](#StreamMisconfigured); a partition outside \[0, Partitions()) is [UnknownPartition](#UnknownPartition).

<a name="Compactor"></a>
## type [Compactor](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

Compactor is the public alias for the sibling that keeps the last record of each key of a partition and drops the older ones, offsets kept.

```go
type Compactor = corestream.Compactor
```

Compactor is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/stream.Compactor`, declared as:

```go
type Compactor interface {
	// Compact removes from partition every keyed record at least
	// [PolicyValue.CompactAfter] old that a later record of the same key, as
	// old, supersedes, and every tombstone at least twice CompactAfter old with
	// them; a record younger than CompactAfter is never touched, and an unkeyed
	// record is left as it is. Every survivor keeps its offset: offsets are
	// never renumbered and [Stream.Bounds] does not move, so a reader inside a
	// compacted range reads on from the next survivor and is refused
	// [OffsetTrimmed] only below the first retained offset, never in a hole.
	//
	// It reports what it looked at — every retained record at least
	// CompactAfter old —, what it kept and what it dropped. A zero CompactAfter
	// never compacts: Compact returns a zero [CompactValue]. A partition outside
	// [0, Partitions()) is [UnknownPartition].
	Compact(ctx context.Context, partition int) (CompactValue, error)
}
```

<a name="Compactor.Compact"></a>
### func \(Compactor\) [Compact](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Compactor) Compact(ctx context.Context, partition int) (CompactValue, error)
```

Compact removes from partition every keyed record at least \[PolicyValue.CompactAfter] old that a later record of the same key, as old, supersedes, and every tombstone at least twice CompactAfter old with them; a record younger than CompactAfter is never touched, and an unkeyed record is left as it is. Every survivor keeps its offset: offsets are never renumbered and [Stream.Bounds](#Stream.Bounds) does not move, so a reader inside a compacted range reads on from the next survivor and is refused [OffsetTrimmed](#OffsetTrimmed) only below the first retained offset, never in a hole.

It reports what it looked at — every retained record at least CompactAfter old —, what it kept and what it dropped. A zero CompactAfter never compacts: Compact returns a zero \[CompactValue]. A partition outside \[0, Partitions()) is [UnknownPartition](#UnknownPartition).

type FileConfig struct {

	// [corestream.PolicyValue].RetainFor, and times the wait
	// [corestream.PolicyValue].BlockTimeout allows. The instants are kept

<a name="Policy"></a>
## type [Policy](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

Policy is the public alias for what a stream enforces: its partitions, its record bound, its retention, its backpressure, its segment size and its compaction window. Its zero value works.

```go
type Policy = corestream.PolicyValue
```

Policy is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/stream.PolicyValue`, declared as:

```go
type Policy struct {
	// Partitions is how many partitions the stream has, fixed for its life.
	// Zero means one; negative is refused.
	Partitions     int
	// MaxRecordBytes bounds one record, its key and payload together. A
	// larger record is refused at [Stream.Append] with [RecordTooLarge]. Zero
	// means [DefaultMaxRecordBytes]; negative is refused.
	MaxRecordBytes int
	// RetainFor is how long a record is kept, measured from its
	// [EntryValue.AppendedAt]: older records are trimmed by the engine, a
	// file engine dropping whole segments only. Zero keeps every record for
	// good; negative is refused.
	RetainFor      time.Duration
	// RetainBytes is how many bytes of records a partition keeps: above it
	// the engine trims the oldest. Zero is unbounded; negative is refused.
	RetainBytes    int64
	// MaxBytes is how many bytes of records the stream may hold before
	// [Stream.Append] waits for room — the producers' backpressure, for a
	// stream whose retention is bounded by its readers rather than by time.
	// Zero is unbounded; negative is refused, and so is a positive value
	// below the normalized MaxRecordBytes, under which no record could fit.
	MaxBytes       int64
	// BlockTimeout is how long an Append waits for room under MaxBytes before
	// it is refused with [StreamFull]. Zero refuses at once. Negative is
	// refused, and so is a positive value with no MaxBytes, which would wait
	// for nothing.
	BlockTimeout   time.Duration
	// SegmentBytes is the size of the segments a file engine writes, and the
	// unit its retention releases. Zero means [DefaultSegmentBytes]; negative
	// is refused. Engines that keep no segments ignore it.
	SegmentBytes   int64
	// CompactAfter is how old a record must be before a [Compactor] may
	// drop it, measured from its [EntryValue.AppendedAt]: a reader that
	// stays within that window behind the head sees every update, and a
	// tombstone is kept one more CompactAfter after it became compactable.
	// Zero never compacts; negative is refused.
	CompactAfter   time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Policy.Normalized"></a>
### func \(Policy\) [Normalized](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/policy.go>)

```go
func (Policy) Normalized() PolicyValue
```

Normalized returns the policy with its clamped fields resolved, so that every engine reads the same numbers rather than each applying the same default. It does NOT validate: call \[PolicyValue.Validate] first, at construction.

<a name="Policy.Validate"></a>
### func \(Policy\) [Validate](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/policy.go>)

```go
func (Policy) Validate() error
```

Validate reports whether the policy is one an engine can honour, and refuses it BY FIELD ([StreamMisconfigured](#StreamMisconfigured), the "field" field naming which) when it is not.

It lives in core so that the memory, file and SQL engines refuse identical inputs identically, which is what makes the first usable as a test double for the other two.

<a name="SQLConfig"></a>
## type [SQLConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

SQLConfig is the public alias for what [NewSQL](#NewSQL) is configured with.

```go

```

SQLConfig is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/stream.SQLConfig`, declared as:

```go
type SQLConfig struct {
	// Transactor is the transaction manager of the database the stream
	// lives in — the one the caller's own transactions are opened with, so
	// a call made under one of them joins it. It must also be a
	// core/data/sql Joiner and Deferrer, which the SDK's own transactor
	// is: the first is how an Append or a Commit joins the caller's
	// transaction, the second how the Waker fires only once that
	// transaction has committed.
	Transactor coresql.Transactor
	// Dialect is the engine's, and must be the Transactor's own: the SQL
	// the stream speaks to it.
	Dialect    coresql.Dialect
	// Table names the records' table; the heads and the cursors are kept
	// in Table__heads and Table__cursors, which [SQLMigration] creates
	// with it. It is a lower-case SQL identifier of at most 54 bytes —
	// PostgreSQL's 63 less the longest suffix —, words of letters and
	// digits joined by single underscores, starting with a letter and not
	// with "sqlite_". Two streams over one database and one Table, in one
	// process or in twenty, are ONE stream.
	Table      string
	// Policy is what the stream enforces; its zero value works. Its
	// RetainBytes and MaxBytes must be zero: the engine keeps no byte
	// count. Its Partitions must stay the same for the life of the
	// tables: a key's partition is its hash modulo that number.
	Policy     corestream.PolicyValue
	// Clock stamps [corestream.EntryValue].AppendedAt and ages records for
	// [corestream.PolicyValue].RetainFor. The instants are the ENGINE's,
	// never the database's NOW(), so a test drives retention with a
	// ManualClock; engines in several processes over one table compare
	// instants their own clocks wrote, and a batch is never stamped before
	// the partition's previous one. Nil means clock.System.
	Clock      clock.Clock
}
```

<a name="Stream"></a>
## type [Stream](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

Stream is the public alias for one named, partitioned log. It is FROZEN at four methods — Append, Read, Bounds, Partitions —; capabilities arrive as siblings ([Waker](#Waker), [Seeker](#Seeker), [Trimmer](#Trimmer), [Compactor](#Compactor), [Committer](#Committer)) reached by type assertion, and every engine here implements all five.

```go
type Stream = corestream.Stream
```

Stream is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/stream.Stream`, declared as:

```go
type Stream interface {
	// Append writes records to one partition as one batch and returns where
	// they landed.
	//
	// The partition is the records' keys': [PartitionOf] of the first keyed
	// record, every other keyed record required to hash to the same partition
	// ([PartitionsMixed] otherwise, nothing written), and an unkeyed record
	// following the batch. A batch with no key at all goes to the partitions in
	// turn. The records take consecutive offsets in their order.
	//
	// When it returns nil, a durable implementation has flushed the whole batch
	// to its device under one sync: a crash one instruction later loses none of
	// it, and a crash before loses all of it, never a part. An implementation
	// that joins the transaction ctx carries (ADR 0151) has instead made the
	// batch part of that transaction.
	//
	// An empty batch is [InvalidBatchSize]; a record whose key and payload
	// together exceed [PolicyValue.MaxRecordBytes] is [RecordTooLarge], the
	// whole batch refused. A stream holding [PolicyValue.MaxBytes] waits up to
	// [PolicyValue.BlockTimeout] for retention to make room, then refuses with
	// [StreamFull]; ctx ends the wait earlier with its own cause.
	Append(ctx context.Context, records []RecordValue) (AppendValue, error)
	// Bounds returns the first offset partition still retains and the next one
	// it will assign. A partition outside [0, Partitions()) is
	// [UnknownPartition].
	Bounds(ctx context.Context, partition int) (BoundsValue, error)
	// Partitions returns how many partitions the stream has, at least one. It
	// never changes for the life of a stream: a key's partition is its hash
	// modulo this number, and changing it would move every key.
	Partitions() int
	// Read returns up to max entries of partition, from offset from on, in
	// offset order. It does NOT block waiting for records: a read at the
	// partition's next offset yields an empty slice and a nil error, and
	// waiting is the caller's ([Waker] tells it when to look again). The
	// offsets a [Compactor] emptied are skipped: the entries carry their own
	// offsets, which need not be consecutive.
	//
	// from below the partition's first retained offset is [OffsetTrimmed] —
	// the records are gone, and silently starting later would hide the gap; one
	// past the next offset is [OffsetAhead]. A partition outside
	// [0, Partitions()) is [UnknownPartition], and a non-positive max is
	// [InvalidBatchSize].
	Read(ctx context.Context, partition int, from Offset, max int) ([]EntryValue, error)
}
```

<a name="Stream.Append"></a>
### func \(Stream\) [Append](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Stream) Append(ctx context.Context, records []RecordValue) (AppendValue, error)
```

Append writes records to one partition as one batch and returns where they landed.

The partition is the records' keys': [PartitionOf](#PartitionOf) of the first keyed record, every other keyed record required to hash to the same partition ([PartitionsMixed](#PartitionsMixed) otherwise, nothing written), and an unkeyed record following the batch. A batch with no key at all goes to the partitions in turn. The records take consecutive offsets in their order.

When it returns nil, a durable implementation has flushed the whole batch to its device under one sync: a crash one instruction later loses none of it, and a crash before loses all of it, never a part. An implementation that joins the transaction ctx carries (ADR 0151) has instead made the batch part of that transaction.

An empty batch is [InvalidBatchSize](#InvalidBatchSize); a record whose key and payload together exceed \[PolicyValue.MaxRecordBytes] is [RecordTooLarge](#RecordTooLarge), the whole batch refused. A stream holding \[PolicyValue.MaxBytes] waits up to \[PolicyValue.BlockTimeout] for retention to make room, then refuses with [StreamFull](#StreamFull); ctx ends the wait earlier with its own cause.

<a name="Stream.Bounds"></a>
### func \(Stream\) [Bounds](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Stream) Bounds(ctx context.Context, partition int) (BoundsValue, error)
```

Bounds returns the first offset partition still retains and the next one it will assign. A partition outside \[0, Partitions()) is [UnknownPartition](#UnknownPartition).

<a name="Stream.Partitions"></a>
### func \(Stream\) [Partitions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Stream) Partitions() int
```

Partitions returns how many partitions the stream has, at least one. It never changes for the life of a stream: a key's partition is its hash modulo this number, and changing it would move every key.

<a name="Stream.Read"></a>
### func \(Stream\) [Read](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Stream) Read(ctx context.Context, partition int, from Offset, max int) ([]EntryValue, error)
```

Read returns up to max entries of partition, from offset from on, in offset order. It does NOT block waiting for records: a read at the partition's next offset yields an empty slice and a nil error, and waiting is the caller's ([Waker](#Waker) tells it when to look again). The offsets a [Compactor](#Compactor) emptied are skipped: the entries carry their own offsets, which need not be consecutive.

from below the partition's first retained offset is [OffsetTrimmed](#OffsetTrimmed) — the records are gone, and silently starting later would hide the gap; one past the next offset is [OffsetAhead](#OffsetAhead). A partition outside \[0, Partitions()) is [UnknownPartition](#UnknownPartition), and a non-positive max is [InvalidBatchSize](#InvalidBatchSize).

<a name="SubscriberConfig"></a>
## type [SubscriberConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

SubscriberConfig is the public alias for what [Subscribe](#Subscribe) is configured with: the group, the handler and its idempotence, the partitions, the commit mode, the retry, the park and the fence.

```go

```

SubscriberConfig is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/stream.SubscriberConfig`, declared as:

```go
type SubscriberConfig struct {
	// BatchSize is the most records one Read hands the handler. Below 1
	// it is read as 1.
	BatchSize           int
	// Clock times the idle wait, the retry wait, the bound on what is sent
	// past a stop and the fence's renewals. Nil means clock.System;
	// nothing in the subscriber calls time.Sleep.
	Clock               clock.Timed
	// Commit is who moves the offset past an accepted batch:
	// [CommitAfterHandler], the zero, or [CommitByHandler]. Any other
	// value is refused.
	Commit              CommitMode
	// Fence, when set, makes each worker hold the lock
	// "stream:<Name>:<Group>:<partition>" while it reads its partition,
	// so the same group in two processes never reads one partition
	// twice at once. Nil fences nothing: one process runs the group.
	Fence               corelock.Locker
	// Group names the consumer group whose offsets are read and
	// committed. It must not be empty; two groups over one stream read
	// every record each, at their own pace.
	Group               string
	// Handler processes each batch. It must be non-nil.
	Handler             Handler
	// HandlerIsIdempotent asserts, in code, that Handler is safe to run
	// more than once for the same records. It must be true; its zero is
	// refused, as queue.ConsumerConfig's is: under [CommitAfterHandler]
	// a batch is delivered at least once, and under [CommitByHandler]
	// the assertion is that the handler's effect and its commit are one
	// transaction, which the SDK cannot see either.
	HandlerIsIdempotent bool
	// Name names the stream in the fence's lock names. It is required
	// when Fence is set, and read for nothing else.
	Name                string
	// Park, when set, sends a record its handler keeps refusing to a
	// queue and moves past it. Nil retries forever: the partition stays
	// blocked until the handler accepts.
	Park                *ParkConfig
	// Partitions are the partitions this subscriber reads, one worker
	// each: static assignment, two processes splitting a group naming
	// disjoint sets (or both every partition, under Fence). Empty means
	// every partition of the stream; a partition outside it, or named
	// twice, is refused.
	Partitions          []int
	// PollInterval bounds how long an idle worker waits before reading
	// again: the stream's Waker ends the wait at once on an Append in this
	// process, so it bounds only what another process appended. Zero, or
	// negative, means 100 ms.
	PollInterval        time.Duration
	// Retry is the wait between two deliveries of a refused batch, its
	// attempt counting the consecutive refusals. A zero BaseDelay means
	// 100 ms doubling to 30 s with a fifth of jitter: a curve with no wait
	// would spin on a failing handler.
	Retry               backoff.Value
	// SettleTimeout bounds each commit, dead letter and fence release
	// sent once ctx has ended, on Clock. Zero, or negative, means 5 s.
	SettleTimeout       time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Trimmer"></a>
## type [Trimmer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

Trimmer is the public alias for the sibling that drops a partition's records below an offset.

```go
type Trimmer = corestream.Trimmer
```

Trimmer is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/stream.Trimmer`, declared as:

```go
type Trimmer interface {
	// Trim makes before the first offset partition retains: every record below
	// it becomes unreadable at once ([OffsetTrimmed]) and its storage is
	// released when the engine can — a file engine releases whole segments only.
	// A before at or below the first offset changes nothing; one past the next
	// offset is [OffsetAhead]; a partition outside [0, Partitions()) is
	// [UnknownPartition]. Offsets are never reused: the next offset does not
	// move.
	Trim(ctx context.Context, partition int, before Offset) error
}
```

<a name="Trimmer.Trim"></a>
### func \(Trimmer\) [Trim](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/stream/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Trimmer) Trim(ctx context.Context, partition int, before Offset) error
```

Trim makes before the first offset partition retains: every record below it becomes unreadable at once ([OffsetTrimmed](#OffsetTrimmed)) and its storage is released when the engine can — a file engine releases whole segments only. A before at or below the first offset changes nothing; one past the next offset is [OffsetAhead](#OffsetAhead); a partition outside \[0, Partitions()) is [UnknownPartition](#UnknownPartition). Offsets are never reused: the next offset does not move.

<a name="Waker"></a>
## type [Waker](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/stream/gen_facade.go>)

Waker is the public alias for the sibling whose signal is closed by the next Append in this process: what ends an idle reader's wait.

```go
type Waker = corestream.Waker
```

Waker is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/stream.Waker`, declared as:

```go
type Waker interface {
	// Wake returns a channel closed by the next Append through this stream value
	// in this process, to any partition. Call it BEFORE the Read that may come
	// back empty: an append landing between that Read and the wait closes the
	// channel already handed out, so it is not missed.
	Wake() <-chan struct{}
}
```
